quote_la: Nicomedes in Bithyniae, Ariobarzanes in Cappadociae regnum reducti sunt

summary_en: Consul Cn. Pompeius defeated the Marsi in battle.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius consul Marsos acie vicit

summary_en: When the state was oppressed by debt, the praetor A. Sempronius Asellio, because he administered justice in favor of debtors, was killed in the forum by the moneylenders.
quote_la: ab his, qui faenerabant, in foro occisus est

summary_en: The book also contains incursions of the Thracians into Macedonia and their ravagings.
quote_la: praeterea incursiones Thracum in Macedoniam populationesque continet

summary_en: The legate A. Postumius Albinus, while commanding the fleet, was killed by his own army on a disgraceful charge of treason.
quote_la: infamis crimine proditionis ab exercitu suo interfectus est

summary_en: The legate L. Cornelius Sulla defeated the Samnites in battle and stormed two of their camps.
quote_la: L. Cornelius Sylla legatus Samnites proelio vicit et bina castra eorum expugnavit

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius received the Vestini in surrender.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius Vestinos in deditionem accepit

summary_en: Consul L. Porcius, after successful operations and repeatedly routing the Marsi, fell while storming their camp, and this gave the enemy the victory in that battle.
quote_la: dum castra eorum expugnat, cecidit

summary_en: Cosconius and Lucceius defeated the Samnites in battle, killed Marius Egnatius, the noblest of the enemy leaders, and received several of their towns in surrender.
quote_la: Marium Egnatium, nobilissimum hostium ducem, occiderunt

summary_en: L. Sulla subdued the Hirpini, routed the Samnites in several battles, received back some peoples, and set out for Rome to seek the consulship with achievements rarely matched by anyone before a consulship.
quote_la: L. Sylla Hirpinos domuit, Samnites pluribus proeliis fudit

summary_en: The legate A. Gabinius, after successful operations against the Lucani and the storming of very many towns, fell in the siege of the enemy's camp.
quote_la: in obsidione hostium castrorum cecidit

summary_en: The legate Sulpicius cut down the Marrucini and recovered that whole region.
quote_la: Sulpicius legatus Marrucinos cecidit, totamque eam regionem recepit

summary_en: Proconsul Cn. Pompeius received the Vestini and Paeligni in surrender.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius pro cos. Vestinos et Paelignos in deditionem accepit

summary_en: The Marsi too, broken in several battles by the legates L. Cinna and Caecilius Pius, began to sue for peace.
quote_la: Marsi quoque a L. Cinna et Caecilio Pio legatis aliquot proeliis fracti petere pacem coeperunt

summary_en: Asculum was captured by Cn. Pompeius.
quote_la: Asculum a Cn. Pompeio captum est

summary_en: With the Italians also cut down by the legate Mamercus Aemilius, Poppaedius Silo, leader of the Marsi and instigator of the affair, fell in battle.
quote_la: Silo Poppaedius dux Marsorum, auctor eius rei, in proelio cecidit

summary_en: Ariobarzanes was driven from the kingdom of Cappadocia and Nicomedes from that of Bithynia by Mithridates, king of Pontus.
quote_la: Ariobarzanes Cappadociae, Nicomedes Bithyniae regno a Mithridate Ponti rege pulsi sunt

summary_en: The book also contains incursions of the Thracians into Macedonia and their ravagings.
quote_la: praeterea incursiones Thracum in Macedoniam populationesque continet

summary_en: Tribune P. Sulpicius, at the instigation of C. Marius, promulgated pernicious laws: that exiles be recalled, new citizens and freedmen be distributed into the thirty-five tribes, and C. Marius be made commander against Mithridates king of Pontus.
quote_la: ut exules revocarentur et novi cives libertinique in tribus XXXV distribuerentur

summary_en: After Sulpicius used violence against the opposing consuls and Q. Pompeius, son of consul Q. Pompeius and son-in-law of Sulla, was killed, consul L. Sulla came into the city with an army, fought in the city itself against the faction of Sulpicius and Marius, and drove it out.
quote_la: L. Sylla consul cum exercitu in urbem venit et adversus factionem Sulpicii et Marii in ipsa urbe pugnavit, eamque expulit

summary_en: Twelve men of that faction, among them C. Marius father and son, were judged public enemies by the senate.
quote_la: ex qua duodecim a senatu hostes, inter quos C. Marius pater et filius, iudicati sunt

summary_en: P. Sulpicius, hiding in a villa, was dragged out on the information of his own slave and killed; the slave, freed so that he might have the promised reward, was then thrown from the rock for the crime of betraying his master.
quote_la: indicio servi sui retractus et occisus est

summary_en: C. Marius the son crossed over to Africa.
quote_la: C. Marius filius in Africam traiecit

summary_en: C. Marius the father, hiding in the marshes of Minturnae, was dragged out by the townsmen; when a Gallic slave sent to kill him drew back in terror at the majesty of so great a man, Marius was placed on a public ship and carried to Africa.
quote_la: missus ad occidendum eum servus natione Gallus maiestate tanti viri perterritus recessisset

summary_en: L. Sulla set in order the constitution of the state and then led out colonies.
quote_la: L. Sylla civitatis statum ordinavit, exinde colonias deduxit

summary_en: Consul Q. Pompeius, having set out to receive the army from proconsul Cn. Pompeius, was killed by the latter's design.
quote_la: ad accipiendum a Cn. Pompeio procos. exercitum profectus, consilio eius occisus est

summary_en: Mithridates, king of Pontus, having seized Bithynia and Cappadocia and driven out the legate Aquilius, entered Phrygia, a province of the Roman people, with a huge army.
quote_la: Phrygiam, provinciam populi Romani, cum ingenti exercitu intravit

summary_en: Mithridates seized Asia and threw the proconsul Q. Oppius and likewise the legate Aquilius into chains.
quote_la: Q. Oppium procos., item Aquilium legatum in vincula coniecit

summary_en: By Mithridates's order, whatever Roman citizens there were in Asia were massacred in a single day.
quote_la: quidquid civium Romanorum in Asia fuit, uno die trucidatum est

summary_en: Mithridates attacked the city of Rhodes, which alone had remained loyal to the Roman people, and after being defeated in several naval battles he withdrew.
quote_la: urbem Rhodum, quae sola in fide populi R. manserat, oppugnavit et aliquot proeliis navalibus victus recessit

summary_en: Archelaus, the king's prefect, came into Greece with an army and occupied Athens.
quote_la: Archelaus praefectus regis in Graeciam cum exercitu venit, Athenas occupavit

summary_en: The book also contains the panic of cities and islands, as states were drawn some to Mithridates and others to the Roman people.
quote_la: trepidationem urbium insularumque, aliis ad Mithridatem aliis ad populum Romanum civitates suas trahentibus

summary_en: Consul L. Cornelius Cinna, carrying pernicious laws by violence and arms, was driven from the city by his colleague Cn. Octavius with six tribunes of the plebs and stripped of his command; he then won over the corrupted army of Appius Claudius and made war on the city, summoning C. Marius and other exiles from Africa.
quote_la: corruptum Appii Claudii exercitum in potestatem suam redegit et bellum urbi intulit

summary_en: In this war two brothers, one from Pompeius's army and one from Cinna's, met unknowingly; the victor, recognizing his slain brother as he despoiled him, raised a pyre for him, stabbed himself over it, and was consumed by the same fire.
quote_la: ipse se supra rogum transfodit et eodem igne consumptus est

summary_en: Though the movement could have been crushed at the start, through the duplicity of Cn. Pompeius, who favored both sides, and the sloth of the consul, Cinna and Marius grew strong and besieged the city with four armies, two of which were given to Q. Sertorius and Carbo.
quote_la: quattuor exercitibus, ex quibus duo Q. Sertorio et Carboni dati sunt, urbem circumsederunt

summary_en: Marius stormed the colony of Ostia and cruelly plundered it.
quote_la: Ostiam coloniam Marius expugnavit et crudeliter diripuit

summary_en: Citizenship was granted by the senate to the Italian peoples.
quote_la: Italicis populis a senatu civitas data est

summary_en: The Samnites, who alone were still in arms, joined Cinna and Marius, and the legate Plautius with his army was cut down by them.
quote_la: ab his Plautius legatus cum exercitu caesus est

summary_en: Cinna and Marius with Carbo and Sertorius attacked the Janiculum and retreated, put to flight by the consul Octavius.
quote_la: Laniculum oppugnaverunt et fugati ab Octavio consule recesserunt

summary_en: Marius stormed the colonies of Antium, Aricia, and Lanuvium.
quote_la: Marius Antium et Ariciam et Lanuvium colonias expugnavit

summary_en: With the optimates having no hope of resisting because of the sloth, treachery, and corruption of leaders and soldiers, Cinna and Marius were received into the city and ravaged it as if captured with slaughter and plunder, killing consul Cn. Octavius and butchering all the nobles of the opposite party, including the orator M. Antonius and C. and L. Caesar, whose heads were set on the rostra.
quote_la: Cn. Octavio consule occiso et omnibus adversae partis nobilibus trucidatis

summary_en: The son of Crassus was killed by Fimbria's cavalry; Crassus the father, lest he suffer anything unworthy of his valor, ran himself through with his sword.
quote_la: pater Crassus, ne quid indignum virtute sua pateretur, gladio se transfixit

summary_en: Without any elections, Cinna and Marius declared themselves consuls for the following year.
quote_la: citra ulla comitia consules in sequentem annum se ipsos renuntiaverunt

summary_en: On the very day he entered office Marius ordered the senator Sex. Licinius thrown from the rock, and after committing very many crimes he died on the Ides of January.
quote_la: Marius S. Licinium senatorem de saxo deici iussit

summary_en: L. Sulla besieged and with great effort stormed Athens, which Archelaus, prefect of Mithridates, had occupied, and restored to the city its liberty and what it had possessed.
quote_la: L. Sylla Athenas, quas Archelaus praefectus Mithridatis occupaverat

summary_en: Magnesia, the only city in Asia that had remained loyal, was defended with the utmost valor against Mithridates.
quote_la: Magnesia, quae sola in Asia civitas in fide manserat, summa virtute adversus Mithridaten defensa est

summary_en: The book also contains raids of the Thracians into Macedonia.
quote_la: praeterea excursiones Thracum in Macedoniam continet

summary_en: Sulla defeated in battle the king's forces, which had occupied Macedonia and come into Thessaly, 100,000 of the enemy being slain and their camp also stormed.
quote_la: proelio vicit, caesis hostium centum milibus et castris quoque expugnatis

summary_en: When the war was then renewed, Sulla again routed and destroyed the king's army.
quote_la: renovato deinde bello iterum exercitum regis fudit ac delevit

summary_en: Archelaus with the royal fleet surrendered himself to Sulla.
quote_la: Archelaus cum classe regia Syllae se tradidit

summary_en: Consul L. Valerius Flaccus, Cinna's colleague, sent to succeed Sulla, being hated by his army for his greed, was killed by his own legate C. Fimbria, a man of utter recklessness, and the command was transferred to Fimbria.
quote_la: a C. Fimbria legato ipsius, ultimae audaciae homine, occisus est, et imperium ad Fimbriam translatum

summary_en: The book also reports cities in Asia stormed by Mithridates, the province cruelly plundered, and incursions of the Thracians into Macedonia.
quote_la: expugnatae in Asia urbes a Mithridate et crudeliter direpta provincia

summary_en: Flavius Fimbria in Asia, after routing several of Mithridates's prefects in battle, took the city of Pergamum and, having besieged the king, came not far from capturing him.
quote_la: urbem Pergamum cepit, obsessumque regem non multum afuit, quin caperet

summary_en: Fimbria stormed and destroyed the city of Ilium, which was reserving itself for Sulla's authority, and recovered a great part of Asia.
quote_la: urbem Ilium, quae se potestati Syllae reservabat, expugnavit ac delevit

summary_en: Sulla cut down the Thracians in several battles.
quote_la: Sylla compluribus proeliis Thracas cecidit

summary_en: While L. Cinna and Cn. Papirius Carbo, who had made themselves consuls for two years, were preparing war against Sulla, it was brought about through L. Valerius Flaccus, princeps of the senate, and those eager for concord, that envoys be sent to Sulla about peace.
quote_la: ut legati ad Syllam de pace mitterentur

summary_en: Cinna was killed by his own army, which he was forcing against its will to board ships and march against Sulla.
quote_la: Cinna ab exercitu suo, quem invitum cogebat naves conscendere et adversus Syllam proficisci, interfectus est

summary_en: Carbo held the consulship alone.
quote_la: consulatum Carbo solus gessit

summary_en: Sulla, having crossed into Asia, made peace with Mithridates on condition that he withdraw from the provinces of Asia, Bithynia, and Cappadocia.
quote_la: pacem cum Mithridate fecit ita, ut his cederet provinciis: Asia, Bithynia, Cappadocia

summary_en: Fimbria, deserted by his army which had gone over to Sulla, stabbed himself and, offering his neck, prevailed on his own slave to kill him.
quote_la: Fimbria desertus ab exercitu, qui ad Syllam transierat, ipse se percussit

summary_en: Sulla replied to the envoys sent by the senate that he would place himself in the senate's power if the citizens who had been driven out by Cinna and had fled to him were restored; though the condition seemed just to the senate, Carbo and his faction, to whom war seemed more useful, prevented agreement.
quote_la: futurum se in potestate senatus respondit, si cives, qui pulsi a Cinna ad se confugerant, restituerentur

summary_en: When the same Carbo wished to exact hostages from all the towns and colonies of Italy to bind their loyalty against Sulla, he was prevented by the unanimous will of the senate.
quote_la: ab omnibus Italiae oppidis coloniisque obsides exigere vellet

summary_en: By decree of the senate the vote was given to the new citizens.
quote_la: novis civibus senatus consulto suffragium datum est

summary_en: Q. Metellus Pius, who had followed the side of the optimates, while stirring up war in Africa, was driven out by the praetor C. Fabius.
quote_la: cum in Africa bellum moliretur, a C. Fabio praetore pulsus est

summary_en: A decree of the senate was carried by the faction of Carbo and the Marian party that all armies everywhere be disbanded.
quote_la: ut omnes ubique exercitus dimitterentur

summary_en: The freedmen were distributed into the thirty-five tribes.
quote_la: libertini in quinque et triginta tribus distributi sunt

summary_en: The book also contains the preparation for the war that was being stirred up against Sulla.
quote_la: praeterea belli apparatum, quod contra Syllam excitabatur, continet

summary_en: Sulla crossed into Italy with his army, and when the envoys he sent to negotiate peace were maltreated by consul C. Norbanus, he defeated that same Norbanus in battle.
quote_la: et ab consule C. Norbano violatis eundem Norbanum proelio vicit

summary_en: When Sulla was about to attack the camp of the other consul, L. Scipio, with whom he had tried in every way and failed to conclude peace, the consul's entire army, won over by soldiers sent out by Sulla, carried its standards over to Sulla.
quote_la: universus exercitus consulis sollicitatus per emissos a Sylla milites signa ad Syllam transtulit

summary_en: Scipio, though he could have been killed, was let go.
quote_la: Scipio cum occidi posset, dimissus est

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, son of the Cn. Pompeius who had taken Asculum, enrolled an army of volunteers and came to Sulla with three legions, to whom all the nobility was flocking, so that the city was deserted as men came to his camp.
quote_la: conscripto voluntariorum exercitu cum tribus legionibus ad Syllam venerat

summary_en: The book also reports expeditions by the generals of both sides throughout all Italy.
quote_la: praeterea expeditiones per totam Italiam utriusque partis ducum referuntur

summary_en: C. Marius, son of C. Marius, was made consul by force before the age of twenty.
quote_la: cum C. Marius C. Marii filius consul ante annos XX per vim creatus esset

summary_en: C. Fabius was burned alive in his headquarters in Africa on account of his cruelty and avarice.
quote_la: C. Fabius in Africa propter crudelitatem et avaritiam suam in praetorio suo vivus exustus est

summary_en: L. Philippus, Sulla's legate, seized Sardinia after the praetor Q. Antonius was driven out and killed.
quote_la: L. Philippus legatus Syllae Sardiniam Q. Antonio praetore pulso et occiso occupavit

summary_en: Sulla struck a treaty with the Italian peoples so that they would not fear he would take away the citizenship and voting rights recently given.
quote_la: Sylla cum Italicis populis, ne timeretur ab his velut erepturus civitatem et suffragii ius nuper datum, foedus percussit

summary_en: Confident of certain victory, Sulla ordered litigants who approached him to carry their recognizances to Rome, although the city was still held by the opposing party.
quote_la: litigatores, a quibus adibatur, vadimonia Romam deferre iussit, cum a parte diversa urbs adhuc teneretur

summary_en: The praetor L. Damasippus, by the will of the consul C. Marius, convened the senate and slaughtered all the nobility that was in the city.
quote_la: L. Damasippus praetor ex voluntate C. Marii consulis cum senatum contraxisset, omnem, quae in urbe erat, nobilitatem trucidavit

summary_en: Among them Q. Mucius Scaevola the pontifex maximus was killed while fleeing in the vestibule of the temple of Vesta.
quote_la: Q. Mucius Scaevola pontifex maximus fugiens in vestibulo aedis Vestae occisus est

summary_en: The book also contains the war renewed by L. Murena against Mithridates in Asia.
quote_la: bellum a L. Murena adversus Mithridaten in Asia renovatum continet

summary_en: Sulla routed and destroyed the army of C. Marius at Sacriportus and besieged him in the town of Praeneste.
quote_la: Sylla C. Marium, exercitu eius fuso deletoque ad Sacriportum, in oppido Praeneste obsedit

summary_en: Sulla recovered the city of Rome from the hands of his enemies.
quote_la: urbem Romam ex inimicorum manibus recepit

summary_en: Sulla repulsed Marius when he attempted to break out.
quote_la: Marium erumpere temptantem reppulit

summary_en: The book also contains the operations of Sulla's legates, with the same fortune for his party everywhere.
quote_la: praeterea res a legatis eius eadem ubique foruna partium gestas continet

summary_en: Sulla drove Carbo out of Italy after cutting down his army at Clusium, Faventia, and Fidentia.
quote_la: Sylla Carbonem, eius exercitu ad Clusium, ad Faventiam Fidentiamque caeso, Italia expulit

summary_en: Sulla finished the war with the Samnites, the only Italian people not yet to have laid down arms, near Rome before the Colline Gate.
quote_la: cum Samnitibus, qui soli ex Italicis populis nondum arma posuerant, iuxta urbem Romanam ante portam Collinam debellavit

summary_en: After the state was recovered, Sulla stained his splendid victory with unparalleled cruelty, slaughtering eight thousand men who had surrendered in the Villa Publica.
quote_la: octo milia dediticiorum in villa publica trucidavit

summary_en: Sulla posted a proscription list and filled the city and all Italy with slaughter.
quote_la: tabulam proscriptionis posuit, urbem ac totam Italiam caedibus replevit

summary_en: Sulla ordered all the unarmed Praenestines to be cut down.
quote_la: omnes Praenestinos inermes concidi iussit

summary_en: Sulla killed Marius, a man of senatorial rank, after his legs and arms were broken, his ears cut off, and his eyes gouged out.
quote_la: Marium, senatorii ordinis virum, cruribus bracchiisque fractis, auribus praesectis et oculis effossis necavit

summary_en: C. Marius, besieged at Praeneste by Lucretius Afella of the Sullan party, took his own life while trying to escape through a tunnel blocked by the army.
quote_la: C. Marius Praeneste obsessus a Lucretio Afella, Syllanarum partium viro, cum per cuniculum captaret evadere saeptum exercitu, mortem conscivit

summary_en: M. Brutus, sent by Cn. Papirius Carbo from Cossyra in a fishing boat to Lilybaeum to find whether Pompeius was there, was surrounded by Pompeius's ships and killed himself by falling on his sword against a thwart of the ship.
quote_la: M. Brutus a Cn. Papirio Carbone, qui Cossyram adpulerat, missus nave piscatoria Lilybaeum

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, sent to Sicily with imperium by the senate, captured and killed Cn. Carbo, who bore his death weeping like a woman.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius in Siciliam cum imperio a senatu missus Cn. Carbonem, qui flens muliebriter mortem tulit, captum occidit

summary_en: Sulla was made dictator and proceeded with twenty-four fasces, which no one had ever done.
quote_la: Sylla dictator factus, quod nemo umquam fecerat, cum fascibus viginti quattuor processit

summary_en: Sulla confirmed the condition of the state with new laws, diminished the power of the tribunes of the plebs, and took away their entire right of proposing laws.
quote_la: legibus novis rei publicae statum confirmavit, tribunorum plebis potestatem minuit et omne ius legum ferendarum ademit

summary_en: Sulla enlarged the colleges of pontiffs and augurs so that there were fifteen members.
quote_la: pontificum augurmque collegium ampliavit, ut essent quindecim

summary_en: Sulla filled up the senate from the equestrian order.
quote_la: senatum ex equestri ordine supplevit

summary_en: Sulla stripped the children of the proscribed of the right to seek office and sold their goods, seizing much for himself; the sum realized was sestertium ter milies quingenties (350,000,000 sesterces).
quote_la: proscriptorum liberis ius petendorum honorum eripuit et bona eorum vendidit, ex quibus plurima [prima] rapuit. redactum est sestertium ter milies quingenties

summary_en: Sulla ordered Q. Lucretius Afella killed in the forum for daring to seek the consulship against his will, and told the assembled Roman people, who took it badly, that he had ordered it.
quote_la: Q. Lucretium Afellam adversus voluntatem suam consulatum petere ausum iussit occidi in foro

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius in Africa defeated and killed the proscribed Cn. Domitius and Hierta, king of Numidia, who were stirring up war.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius in Africa Cn. Domitium proscriptum et Hiertam, regem Numidiae, bellum molientes victos occidit

summary_en: At twenty-four years of age, while still a Roman knight, Pompeius triumphed from Africa, which had fallen to no one before.
quote_la: quattuor et viginti annos natus, adhuc eques Romanus, quod nulli contigerat, ex Africa triumphavit

summary_en: C. Norbanus, a proscribed ex-consul, killed himself in the city of Rhodes when he was about to be apprehended.
quote_la: C. Norbanus consularis proscriptus in urbe Rhodo cum comprehenderetur, ipse se occidit

summary_en: Mutilus, one of the proscribed, secretly came with covered head to the back door of his wife Bastia, was refused admission because she said he was proscribed, and stabbed himself, spattering her doors with his blood.
quote_la: Mutilus, unus ex proscriptis, clam capite adoperto ad posticias aedes Bastiae uxoris cum accessisset, admissus non est

summary_en: Sulla recovered Aesernia in Samnium.
quote_la: Sylla Aeserniam in Samnio recepit

summary_en: Sulla settled XLVII (forty-seven) legions on captured lands and divided the lands among them.
quote_la: XLVII legiones in agros captos deduxit et eos his divisit

summary_en: Sulla besieged Volaterrae, a town still in arms, and received its surrender.
quote_la: Volaterras, quod oppidum adhuc in armis erat, obsessum in deditionem accepit

summary_en: Mytilene in Asia, the only city still retaining arms after the defeat of Mithridates, was stormed and destroyed.
quote_la: Mitylenae quoque in Asia, quae sola urbs post victum Mithridaten arma retinebat, expugnatae dirutaeque sunt

summary_en: Sulla died, and the senate granted him the honor of burial in the Campus Martius.
quote_la: Sylla decessit, honosque ei a senatu habitus est, ut in campo Martio sepeliretur

summary_en: M. Lepidus stirred up war when he tried to rescind Sulla's acts.
quote_la: M. Lepidus cum acta Syllae temptaret rescindere, bellum excitavit

summary_en: Lepidus was driven from Italy by his colleague Q. Catulus and perished in Sardinia after vainly attempting war.
quote_la: a Q. Catulo collega Italia pulsus et in Sardinia frustra bellum molitus perit

summary_en: M. Brutus, who held Cisalpine Gaul, was killed by Cn. Pompeius.
quote_la: M. Brutus, qui Cisalpinam Galliam obtinebat, a Cn. Pompeio occisus est

summary_en: The proscribed Q. Sertorius stirred up an enormous war in Further Spain.
quote_la: Q. Sertorius proscriptus in ulteriore Hispania ingens bellum excitavit

summary_en: The proconsul L. Manlius and the legate M. Domitius were defeated in battle by the quaestor Hirtuleius.
quote_la: L. Manlius proconsul et M. Domitius legatus ab Hirtuleio quaestore proelio victi sunt

summary_en: The book also contains the operations of the proconsul P. Servilius against the Cilicians.
quote_la: res a P. Servilio procos adversus Cilicas gestas continet

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, while still a Roman knight, was sent with consular imperium against Sertorius.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius cum adhuc eques Romanus esset, cum imperio consulari adversus Sertorium missus est

summary_en: Sertorius stormed several cities and brought very many states under his power.
quote_la: Sertorius aliquot urbes expugnavit plurimasque civitates in potestatem suam redegit

summary_en: The proconsul Appius Claudius defeated the Thracians in several battles.
quote_la: Appius Claudius procos. Thracas pluribus proeliis vicit

summary_en: The proconsul Q. Metellus cut down L. Hirtuleius, Sertorius's quaestor, together with his army.
quote_la: Q. Metellus pro cos. L. Hirtuleium quaestorem Sertorii cum exercitu cecidit

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius fought an indecisive battle with Sertorius, in which each side was victorious on one wing.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius dubio eventu cum Sertorio pugnavit, ita ut singula ex utraque parte cornua vicerint

summary_en: Q. Metellus routed Sertorius and Perperna with their two armies in battle.
quote_la: Q. Metellus Sertorium et Perpernam cum duobus exercitibus proelio fudit

summary_en: Pompeius, wishing to take a share of that victory, fought with little success.
quote_la: cuius victoriae partem cupiens ferre Pompeius parum prospere pugnavit

summary_en: Sertorius, then besieged at Clunia, inflicted no lighter losses on the besiegers by constant sorties.
quote_la: obsessus deinde Cluniae Sertorius adsiduis eruptionibus non leviora damna obsidentibus intulit

summary_en: The book also contains the operations of the proconsul Curio in Thrace against the Dardani.
quote_la: res ab Curione procos. in Thracia gestas adversus Dardanos

summary_en: Sertorius committed many cruelties against his own, killing very many of his friends and fellow proscribed on fabricated charges of treason.
quote_la: qui plurimos ex amicis et secum proscriptis crimine proditionis insimulatos occidit

summary_en: The proconsul P. Servilius subdued the Isauri in Cilicia and stormed several cities of the pirates.
quote_la: P. Servilius procos in Cilicia Isauros domuit et aliquot urbes piratarum expugnavit

summary_en: Nicomedes, king of Bithynia, made the Roman people his heir, and his kingdom was reduced to the form of a province.
quote_la: Nicomedes Bithyniae rex populum Romanum fecit heredem, regnumque eius in provinciae formam redactum est

summary_en: Mithridates, having struck a treaty with Sertorius, made war on the Roman people.
quote_la: Mithridates foedere cum Sertorio icto bellum populo Romano intulit

summary_en: Bithynia was occupied, and the consul M. Aurelius Cotta was defeated in battle by the king at Chalcedon.
quote_la: occupata Bithynia M. Aurelius Cotta consul ad Calchedona proelio a rege victus

summary_en: Pompeius and Metellus drove Sertorius's forces from the siege of the town of Calagurris and forced them to seek different regions, Metellus going to Further Spain and Pompeius to Gaul.
quote_la: ab obsidione Calagurris oppidi depulsos coegerit diversas regiones petere, Metellum ulteriorem Hispaniam, Pompeium Galliam

summary_en: The consul L. Licinius Lucullus fought successfully against Mithridates in cavalry battles, carried out several prosperous expeditions, and restrained his soldiers, who were demanding battle, from mutiny.
quote_la: L. Licinius Lucullus consul adversus Mithridaten equestribus proeliis feliciter pugnavit et aliquot expeditiones prosperas fecit

summary_en: Deiotarus, tetrarch of Gallograecia, cut down the prefects of Mithridates who were stirring up war in Phrygia.
quote_la: Deiotarus Gallograeciae tetrarches praefectos Mithridatis bellum in Phrygia moventes cecidit

summary_en: The book also contains the successful operations of Cn. Pompeius in Spain against Sertorius.
quote_la: res a Cn. Pompeio in Hispania contra Sertorium prospere gestas continet

summary_en: The proconsul C. Curio subdued the Dardani in Thrace.
quote_la: C. Curio procos. Dardanos in Thracia domuit

summary_en: Seventy-four gladiators escaped from the school of Lentulus at Capua and gathered a multitude of slaves and workhouse prisoners, stirring up war under the leaders Crixus and Spartacus.
quote_la: quattuor et septuaginta gladiatores Capuae ex ludo Lentuli profugerunt

summary_en: The fugitives defeated the legate Claudius Pulcher and the praetor P. Varenus in battle.
quote_la: Claudium Pulchrum legatum et P. Varenum praetorem proelio vicerunt

summary_en: The proconsul L. Lucullus destroyed Mithridates' army by famine and sword at the city of Cyzicus, and forced the king, driven from Bithynia and broken by various misfortunes of war and shipwrecks, to flee to Pontus.
quote_la: L. Lucullus pro cos. ad Cyzicum urbem exercitum Mithridatis fame ferroque delevit

summary_en: The praetor Q. Arrius cut down Crixus, a leader of the fugitives, together with twenty thousand men.
quote_la: Q. Arrius praetor Crixum fugitivorum ducem cum viginti milibus hominum cecidit

summary_en: The consul Cn. Lentulus fought unsuccessfully against Spartacus.
quote_la: Cn. Lentulus consul male adversus Spartacum pugnavit

summary_en: The consul L. Gellius and the praetor Q. Arrius were defeated in battle by Spartacus.
quote_la: ab eodem L. Gellius consul et Q. Arrius praetor acie victi sunt

summary_en: Sertorius was killed at a banquet by M. Perperna, M'. Antonius, and other conspirators in the eighth year of his command, a great general who had rather often been victorious against the two commanders Pompeius and Metellus, but at the end both savage and prodigal.
quote_la: Sertorius a M. Perperna et M'. Antonio et aliis coniuratis in convivio interfectus est, octavo ducatus sui anno

summary_en: The command of the party passed to Marcus (Perperna), whom Cn. Pompeius defeated, captured, and killed, recovering the Spains in about the tenth year after the war began.
quote_la: imperium partium ad Marcum translatum, quem Cn. Pompeius victum captumque interfecit, ac recepit Hispanias decimo fere anno quam coeptum erat bellum

summary_en: The proconsul C. Cassius and the praetor Cn. Manlius fought unsuccessfully against Spartacus, and that war was entrusted to the praetor M. Crassus.
quote_la: C. Cassius pro cos. et Cn. Manlius praetor male adversus Spartacum pugnaverunt, idque bellum M. Crasso praetori mandatum est

summary_en: The praetor M. Crassus first fought successfully against the part of the fugitives consisting of Gauls and Germans, killing thirty-five thousand of the enemy including their leaders Castus and Gannicus.
quote_la: caesis hostium triginta quinque milibus et ducibus eorum Casto et Gannico

summary_en: Crassus then finished the war with Spartacus, sixty thousand being killed together with him.
quote_la: cum Spartaco dein debellavit, caesis cum ipso sexaginta milibus

summary_en: The praetor M. Antonius ended with his own death the war against the Cretans that he had undertaken with little success.
quote_la: M. Antonius praetor bellum adversus Cretenses parum prospere susceptum morte sua finiit

summary_en: The proconsul M. Lucullus subjugated the Thracians.
quote_la: M. Lucullus pro cos. Thracas subegit

summary_en: L. Lucullus fought successfully against Mithridates in Pontus, more than sixty thousand of the enemy being killed.
quote_la: L. Lucullus in Ponto adversus Mithridaten feliciter pugnavit, caesis hostium amplius quam sexaginta milibus

summary_en: M. Crassus and Cn. Pompeius were made consuls (Pompeius by senatorial decree before holding the quaestorship, direct from Roman knight) and restored the tribunician power.
quote_la: M. Crassus et Cn. Pompeius consules facti (s. c. Pompeius, antequam quaesturam gereret, ex equite Romano) tribuniciam potestatem restituerunt

summary_en: The courts were also transferred to the Roman knights through the praetor M. Aurelius Cotta.
quote_la: iudicia quoque per M. Aurelium Cottam praetorem ad equites Romanos translata sunt

summary_en: Mithridates, driven by despair of his situation, fled to Tigranes, king of Armenia.
quote_la: Mithridates desperatione rerum surarum coactus ad Tigranen Armeniae regem confugit

summary_en: Machares, son of Mithridates and king of Bosporus, was received into friendship by L. Lucullus.
quote_la: Machares filius Mithridatis, Bospori rex, a L. Lucullo in amicitiam receptus est

summary_en: The censors Cn. Lentulus and L. Gellius conducted a harsh censorship, removing sixty-four men from the senate.
quote_la: Cn. Lentulus et L. Gellius censores asperam censuram egerunt quattuor et sexaginta senatu motis

summary_en: When the censors completed the lustrum, DCCCC (900 thousand) citizen heads were registered in the census.
quote_la: a quibus lustro condito censa sunt civium capita DCCCC

summary_en: The praetor L. Metellus operated successfully against the pirates in Sicily.
quote_la: L. Metellus praetor in Sicilia adversus piratas prospere rem gessit

summary_en: The temple of Jupiter on the Capitol, which had been destroyed by fire and rebuilt, was dedicated by Q. Catulus.
quote_la: templum Iovis in Capitolio, quod incendio consumptum ac refectum erat, a Q. Catulo dedicatum est

summary_en: L. Lucullus routed Mithridates and Tigranes and the enormous forces of both kings in several battles in Armenia.
quote_la: L. Lucullus in Armenia Mithridaten et Tigranen et ingentes utriusque regis copias pluribus proeliis fudit

summary_en: The proconsul Q. Metellus, entrusted with the war against the Cretans, besieged the city of Cydonia.
quote_la: Q. Metellus procos. bello adversus Cretenses mandato Cydoniam urbem obsedit

summary_en: C. Triarius, a legate of Lucullus, fought with little success against Mithridates.
quote_la: C. Triarius legatus Luculli adversus Mithridaten parum prospere pugnavit

summary_en: A mutiny of his soldiers, who refused to follow, held Lucullus back from pursuing Mithridates and Tigranes and completing his victory.
quote_la: Lucullum, ne persequeretur Mithridaten ac Tigranen summamque victoriae imponeret, seditio militum tenuit

summary_en: The proconsul Q. Metellus stormed Cnossos, Lyctus, Cydonia, and very many other cities.
quote_la: Q. Metellus procos. Cnoson et Lyctum et Cydoniam et alias plurimas urbes expugnavit

summary_en: The tribune of the plebs L. Roscius carried a law assigning the fourteen nearest rows in the theater to the Roman knights.
quote_la: L. Roscius tribunus plebis legem tulit, ut equitibus Romanis in theatro quattuordecim gradus proximi adsignarentur

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, ordered by a law passed before the people to pursue the pirates who had cut off the grain trade, drove them from the whole sea within the fortieth day.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius lege ad populum lata persequi piratas iussus, qui commercium annonae intercluserant, intra quadragesimum diem toto mari eos expulit

summary_en: Having finished the war with the pirates in Cilicia, Pompeius received them in surrender and gave them lands and cities.
quote_la: belloque cum his in Cilicia confecto, acceptis in deditionem piratis agros et urbes dedit

summary_en: The book contains the exchanged letters of Metellus and Pompeius: Metellus complains that the glory of his achievements is being snatched from him by Pompeius, who sent a legate to Crete to receive the surrender of the cities, and Pompeius gives his reasons for having had to do so.
quote_la: queritur Q. Metellus gloriam sibi rerum a se gestarum a Pompeio praeripi

summary_en: The tribune of the plebs C. Manilius, to the great indignation of the nobility, carried a law entrusting the Mithridatic war to Pompeius.
quote_la: C. Manilius tribunus plebis magna indignatione nobilitatis legem tulit, ut Pompeio Mithridaticum bellum mandaretur

summary_en: Q. Metellus, having completely subdued the Cretans, gave laws to the island, free until that time.
quote_la: Q. Metellus perdomitis Cretensibus liberae in id tempus insulae leges dedit

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, setting out to wage war against Mithridates, renewed friendship with Phraates, king of the Parthians.
quote_la: cum rege Parthorum Prahate amicitiam renovavit

summary_en: Pompeius defeated Mithridates in a cavalry battle.
quote_la: equestri proelio Mithridaten vicit

summary_en: The book also contains the war between Phraates, king of the Parthians, and Tigranes of the Armenians, and then the war waged between the son Tigranes and his father.
quote_la: bellum inter Prahaten Parthorum regem et Tigranen Armeniorum, ac deinde inter filium Tigranen patremque gestum continet

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius defeated Mithridates in a night battle and forced him to flee to Bosporus.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius Mithridaten nocturno proelio victum coegit Bosporum profugere

summary_en: Pompeius received Tigranes in surrender and, having taken away Syria, Phoenicia, and Cilicia, restored to him the kingdom of Armenia.
quote_la: Tigranen in deditionem accepit eique ademptis Syria Phoenice Cilicia regnum Armeniae restituit

summary_en: A conspiracy to kill the consuls, formed by men condemned for electoral bribery in their candidacy for the consulship, was suppressed.
quote_la: coniuratio eorum, qui in petitione consulatus ambitus damnati erant, facta de interficiendis consulibus oppressa est

summary_en: Pompeius, while pursuing Mithridates, penetrated to the most distant and unknown peoples and defeated in battle the Iberians and Albanians, who refused passage.
quote_la: Hiberos Albanosque, qui transitum non dabant, proelio vicit

summary_en: The book also contains the flight of Mithridates through the Colchians and Heniochi and his deeds in Bosporus.
quote_la: fugam Mithridatis per Colchos Heniochosque et res ab eo in Bosporo gestas continet

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius reduced Pontus to the form of a province.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius in provinciae formam Pontum redegit

summary_en: Pharnaces, son of Mithridates, made war on his father.
quote_la: Pharnaces filius Mithridatis bellum patri intulit

summary_en: Mithridates, besieged in his palace by Pharnaces, took poison with too little effect and was killed by a Gallic soldier named Bitocus, whom he had asked to help him die.
quote_la: a milite Gallo nomine Bitoco, a quo ut adiuvaret se petierat, interfectus est

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius subjugated the Jews and took their shrine at Jerusalem, inviolate before that time.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius Iudaeos subegit; fanum eorum Hierosolyma, inviolatum ante id tempus, cepit

summary_en: L. Catilina, having twice suffered defeat in his candidacy for the consulship, conspired with the praetor Lentulus, Cethegus, and many others to slaughter the consuls and senate, burn the city, and crush the republic, with an army also readied in Etruria.
quote_la: cum Lentulo praetore et Cethego et compluribus aliis coniuravit de caede consulum et senatus, incendiis urbis et opprimenda re publica

summary_en: The conspiracy was uncovered by the diligence of M. Tullius Cicero; Catilina was driven from the city and punishment was exacted from the remaining conspirators.
quote_la: ea coniuratio industria M. Tullii Ciceronis eruta est. Catilina urbe pulso de reliquis coniuratis supplicium sumptum est

summary_en: Catilina was cut down with his army by the proconsul C. Antonius.
quote_la: Catilina a C. Antonio procos. cum exercitu caesus est

summary_en: P. Clodius, accused of secretly entering in women's dress a shrine that it is sacrilege for a man to enter, and of debauching the wife of the pontifex Metellus, was acquitted.
quote_la: P. Clodius accusatus, quod in habitu mulieris in sacrarium, [in] quo virum intrare nefas est, clam intrasset

summary_en: The praetor C. Pontinus subdued the Allobroges, who had rebelled, at Solo.
quote_la: C. Pontinus praetor Allobrogas, qui rebellaverant, ad Solonem domuit

summary_en: P. Clodius transferred to the plebs.
quote_la: P. Clodius ad plebem transit

summary_en: C. Caesar subjugated the Lusitanians.
quote_la: C. Caesar Lusitanos subegit

summary_en: When Caesar was a candidate for the consulship and sought to seize control of the state, a conspiracy was formed among the three leading men of the state, Cn. Pompeius, M. Crassus, and C. Caesar.
quote_la: conspiratio inter tres civitatis principes facta est, Cn. Pompeium, M. Crassum, C. Caesarem

summary_en: Agrarian laws were carried by the consul Caesar with great struggle, against the will of the senate and of the other consul M. Bibulus.
quote_la: leges agrariae a Caesare consule cum magna contentione, invito senatu et altero consule M. Bibulo, latae sunt

summary_en: The proconsul C. Antonius operated with little success in Thrace.
quote_la: C. Antonius pro cos. in Thracia parum prospere rem gessit

summary_en: M. Cicero was sent into exile under a law carried by the tribune of the plebs P. Clodius, on the ground that he had put citizens to death uncondemned.
quote_la: M. Cicero lege a P. Clodio tribuno plebis lata, quod indemnatos cives necavisset, in exilium missus est

summary_en: Caesar, having set out for the province of Gaul, subdued the Helvetii, a wandering people that, seeking a home, wanted to march through Caesar's province of Narbonensis.
quote_la: Caesar in provinciam Galliam profectus Helvetios, vagam gentem, domuit

summary_en: The book also contains the geography of the Gauls.
quote_la: praeterea situm Galliarum continet

summary_en: Pompeius triumphed over the children of Mithridates and over Tigranes, son of Tigranes, and was hailed Magnus by the whole assembly.
quote_la: Pompeius de liberis Mithridatis et Tigrane Tigranis filio triumphavit Magnusque a tota contione consalutatus est

summary_en: The first part of the book contains the geography and customs of Germany.
quote_la: prima pars libri situm Germaniae moresque continet

summary_en: C. Caesar, leading his army against the Germans who had crossed into Gaul under Ariovistus, at the request of the Aedui and Sequani whose land was being occupied, checked by an address the panic of his soldiers at the new enemy, defeated the Germans in battle, and drove them from Gaul.
quote_la: trepidationem militum propter metum novorum hostium ortam adlocutione exercitus inhibuit et victos proelio Germanos Gallia expulit

summary_en: M. Cicero was brought back from exile, with Pompeius among others exerting himself and the tribune of the plebs T. Annius Milo acting, to the enormous joy of the senate and all Italy.
quote_la: ingenti gaudio senatus ac totius Italiae ab exilio reductus est

summary_en: The charge of the grain supply was entrusted to Cn. Pompeius for five years.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeio per quinquennium annonae cura mandata est

summary_en: Caesar defeated in battle and received in surrender the Ambiani, Suessiones, Viromandui, and Atrebates, Belgian peoples of enormous numbers.
quote_la: Caesar Ambianos, Suessionas, Viromanduos, Atrebates, Belgarum populos, quorum ingens multitudo erat, proelio victos in deditionem accepit

summary_en: Caesar then fought at great hazard against the Nervii and destroyed that nation, which fought on until of LX armed men only D survived and of DC senators only three escaped.
quote_la: donec ex LX armatorum D superessent, ex DC senatoribus tres tantum evaderent

summary_en: A law was passed for reducing Cyprus to the form of a province and confiscating the royal money, and the administration of the matter was entrusted to M. Cato.
quote_la: lege lata de redigenda in provinciae formam Cypro et publicanda pecunia regia M. Catoni administratio eius rei mandata est

summary_en: Ptolemy, king of Egypt, because of the injuries he suffered from his own people, left his kingdom and came to Rome.
quote_la: Ptolemaeus Aegypti rex ob iniurias, quas patiebatur a suis, relicto regno Romam venit

summary_en: C. Caesar defeated the Veneti, a people bordering the Ocean, in a naval battle.
quote_la: C. Caesar Venetos, gentem Oceano iunctam, navali proelio vicit

summary_en: The book also contains the operations of Caesar's legates, carried out with the same fortune.
quote_la: praeterea res a legatis eius eadem fortuna gestas continet

summary_en: When the elections were being blocked by the vetoes of the tribune of the plebs C. Cato, the senate changed its dress.
quote_la: cum C. Catonis tribuni plebis intercessionibus comitia tollerentur, senatus vestem mutavit

summary_en: M. Cato suffered defeat in his candidacy for the praetorship, Vatinius being preferred.
quote_la: M. Cato in petitione praeturae praelato Vatinio repulsam tulit

summary_en: When Cato obstructed the law by which provinces were given to the consuls for five years—the Spains to Pompeius, Syria and the Parthian war to Crassus—he was led off to prison by the tribune of the plebs C. Trebonius, the author of the law.
quote_la: idem cum legem impediret, qua provinciae consulibus in quinquennium, Pompeio Hispaniae, Crasso Syria et Parthicum bellum dabantur

summary_en: The proconsul A. Gabinius brought Ptolemy back into his kingdom of Egypt, ejecting Archelaus, whom the Egyptians had adopted as their king.
quote_la: A. Gabinius procos. Ptolemaeum reduxit in regnum Aegypti, eiecto Archelao, quem sibi regem adsciverant

summary_en: After defeating the Germans in Gaul, Caesar crossed the Rhine and subdued the nearest part of Germany.
quote_la: victis Germanis in Gallia Caesar Rhenum transcendit et proximam partem Germaniae domuit

summary_en: Caesar then crossed the Ocean to Britain, at first with little success because of adverse storms, a second time more happily, and after killing a great multitude of the enemy brought some part of the island under his power.
quote_la: Oceano in Britanniam primo parum prospere tempestatibus adversis traiecit, iterum felicius

summary_en: Julia, Caesar's daughter and Pompeius's wife, died, and the people granted her the honor of burial in the Campus Martius.
quote_la: Iulia Caesaris filia, Pompeii uxor, decessit, honosque ei a populo habitus est, ut in campo Martio sepeliretur

summary_en: Several Gallic peoples revolted under the leadership of Ambiorix, king of the Eburones, by whom Caesar's legates Cotta and Titurius were ambushed and cut down with the army they commanded.
quote_la: a quibus Cotta et Titurius legati Caesaris circumventi insidiis cum exercitu, cui praeerant, caesi sunt

summary_en: The camps of other legions were also attacked and defended with great effort, and the enemy attacking the camp commanded by Q. Cicero among the Treveri were routed in battle by Caesar himself.
quote_la: cum aliarum quoque legionum castra oppugnata magno labore defensa essent

summary_en: M. Crassus, about to make war on the Parthians, crossed the river Euphrates and was defeated in a battle in which his son also fell.
quote_la: M. Crassus bellum Parthis inlaturus Euphraten flumen transit, victusque proelio, in quo et filius eius cecidit

summary_en: Crassus, having withdrawn the remnants of his army to a hill, was summoned to a parley by the enemy under Surenas as if to treat of peace, was seized, and, resisting so as not to suffer anything alive, was killed.
quote_la: comprehensusque et ne quid vivus pateretur repugnans, interfectus est

summary_en: C. Caesar, after defeating the Treveri in Gaul, crossed a second time into Germany and, finding no enemy there, returned to Gaul.
quote_la: C. Caesar Treveris in Gallia victis iterum in Germaniam transit

summary_en: Caesar defeated the Eburones and the other states that had conspired, and pursued Ambiorix in his flight.
quote_la: reversus in Galliam Eburonas et alias civitates, quae conspiraverant, vicit et Ambiorigem in fuga persecutus est

summary_en: The body of P. Clodius, killed by T. Annius Milo, a candidate for the consulship, on the Appian Way at Bovillae, was cremated by the plebs in the senate house.
quote_la: P. Clodii a T. Annio Milone, candidato consulatus, Appia via ad Bovillas occisi corpus plebs in curia cremavit

summary_en: Amid the violent struggles among the consular candidates Hypsaeus, Scipio, and Milo, Cn. Pompeius was made consul for the third time by the senate to suppress them, in his absence and as sole consul, which had happened to no one else.
quote_la: ad comprimendas eas Cn. Pompeio legato et a senatu consul tertio factus est absens et solus

summary_en: A court of inquiry having been decreed concerning the death of P. Clodius, Milo was condemned at trial and driven into exile.
quote_la: quaestione decreta de morte P. Clodii Milo iudicio damnatus in exilium actus est

summary_en: A law was passed that account be taken of the absent Caesar's candidacy for the consulship, against the will and opposition of M. Cato.
quote_la: lex lata est, ut ratio absentis Caesaris in petitione consulatus haberetur, invito et contra dicente M. Catone

summary_en: The book also contains C. Caesar's operations against the Gauls, who revolted almost universally under the leadership of the Arvernian Vercingetorix, and the laborious sieges of cities, among them Avaricum of the Bituriges and Gergovia of the Arverni.
quote_la: res gestas a C. Caesare adversus Gallos, qui prope universi Vercingetorige Arverno duce defecerunt

summary_en: C. Caesar defeated the Gauls at Alesia and received in surrender all the states of Gaul that had been in arms.
quote_la: C. Caesar Gallos ad Alesiam vicit omnesque Galliae civitates, quae in armis fuerant, in deditionem accepit

summary_en: C. Cassius, quaestor of M. Crassus, cut down the Parthians who had crossed into Syria.
quote_la: C. Cassius, quaestor M. Crassi, Parthos, qui in Syriam transcenderant, cecidit

summary_en: M. Cato suffered defeat in his candidacy for the consulship, Ser. Sulpicius and M. Marcellus being elected consuls.
quote_la: in petitione consulatus M. Cato repulsam tulit, creatis consulibus Ser. Sulpicio M. Marcello

summary_en: Caesar subdued the Bellovaci together with other Gallic peoples.
quote_la: C. Cacsar Bellovacos cum aliis Gallorum populis domuit

summary_en: The book contains the disputes between the consuls about sending a successor to C. Caesar, with the consul M. Marcellus urging in the senate that Caesar come in person to stand for the consulship, although by the law passed he was entitled to hold his provinces until the time of his consulship.
quote_la: contentiones inter consules de successore C. Caesari mittendo

summary_en: The book also contains the operations of M. Bibulus in Syria.
quote_la: resque a M. Bibulo in Syria gestas continet

summary_en: The causes and beginnings of the civil war are related, together with the disputes about sending a successor to C. Caesar, who refused to dismiss his armies unless Pompeius dismissed his.
quote_la: causae civilium armorum et initia referuntur contentionesque de successore C. Caesari mittendo

summary_en: The book contains the actions of the tribune of the plebs C. Curio, first against Caesar and then for Caesar.
quote_la: C. Curionis tribuni plebis primum adversus Caesarem, deinde pro Caesare actiones continet

summary_en: When a decree of the senate was passed that a successor be sent to Caesar, the tribunes of the plebs M. Antonius and Q. Cassius, because they were blocking the decree by their vetoes, were driven from the city, and the senate charged the consuls and Cn. Pompeius to see that the republic took no harm.
quote_la: M. Antonio et Q. Cassio tribunis plebis, quoniam intercessionibus id senatus consultum impediebant, urbe pulsis

summary_en: C. Caesar, intent on pursuing his enemies in war, came into Italy with his army, took Corfinium together with L. Domitius and P. Lentulus, released them, and drove Cn. Pompeius and the rest of his party out of Italy.
quote_la: Corfinium cum L. Domitio et P. Lentulo cepit eosque dimisit, Cn. Pompeium ceterosque partium eius Italia expulit

summary_en: C. Caesar besieged Massilia, which had closed its gates, leaving his legates C. Trebonius and D. Brutus at the siege of the city.
quote_la: C. Caesar Massiliam, quae portas cluserat, obsedit

summary_en: Setting out for Spain, Caesar received in surrender L. Afranius and M. Petreius, legates of Cn. Pompeius, with seven legions at Ilerda, and let them all go unharmed.
quote_la: L. Afranium et M. Petreium legatos Cn. Pompeii cum septem legionibus ad Ilerdam in deditionem accepit omnesque incolumes dimisit

summary_en: Varro too, a legate of Pompeius, was brought with his army into Caesar's power.
quote_la: Varrone quoque legato Pompeii cum exercitu in potestatem suam redacto

summary_en: Caesar gave citizenship to the people of Gades.
quote_la: suam redacto. Gaditanis civitatem dedit

summary_en: The Massilienses, defeated in two naval battles, surrendered themselves to Caesar's power after a long siege.
quote_la: Massilienses duobus navalibus proeliis victi post longam obsidionem potestati Caesarisse permiserunt

summary_en: C. Antonius, a legate of Caesar, after operating unsuccessfully against the Pompeians in Illyricum, was captured.
quote_la: C. Antonius legatus Caesaris male adversus Pompeianos in Illyrico rebus gestis captus est

summary_en: In that war the Opitergini from across the Po, auxiliaries of Caesar, their raft hemmed in by enemy ships, fell fighting one another rather than come into the enemy's power.
quote_la: potius quam in potestatem hostium venirent, inter se concurrentes occubuerunt

summary_en: C. Curio, Caesar's legate in Africa, after fighting successfully against Varus, the commander of the Pompeian party, was cut down with his army by Juba, king of Mauretania.
quote_la: C. Curio, legatus Caesaris in Africa, cum prospere adversus Varum Pompeianarum partium ducem pugnasset, a Iuba rege Mauretaniae cum exercitu caesus est

summary_en: C. Caesar crossed over to Greece.
quote_la: C. Caesar in Graeciam traiecit

summary_en: The praetor M. Caelius Rufus, after stirring sedition in the city by exciting the plebs with hope of debt cancellation, was deposed from office, expelled, and joined the exile Milo, who had gathered an army of fugitives; both were killed while attempting war.
quote_la: abrogato magistratu pulsus urbe Miloni exuli

summary_en: Cleopatra, queen of Egypt, was driven from her kingdom by her brother Ptolemy.
quote_la: Cleopatra regina Aegypti ab Ptolemaeo fratre regno pulsa est

summary_en: Because of the greed and cruelty of the praetor Q. Cassius, the people of Corduba in Spain with two Varronian legions defected from Caesar's side.
quote_la: propter Q. Cassii praetoris avaritiam crudelitatemque

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, besieged by Caesar at Dyrrachium, broke the siege after storming Caesar's garrisons with great slaughter, but when the war was transferred to Thessaly he was defeated in battle at Pharsalus.
quote_la: translato in Thessaliam bello, apud Pharsaliam acie victus est

summary_en: Cicero remained in camp, a man born for nothing less than war.
quote_la: Cicero in castris remansit, vir nihil minus quam ad bella natus

summary_en: Caesar pardoned all of the opposing party who surrendered themselves to the victor's power.
quote_la: omnibusque adversarum partium, qui se potestati victoris permiserant, Caesar ignovit

summary_en: The panic and flight of the defeated party into different parts of the world are related.
quote_la: trepidatio victarum partium in diversas orbis terrarum partes

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, seeking Egypt, was killed by Achillas in a small boat before landing, on the order of king Ptolemy, his ward, at the urging of the tutor Theodotus and of Pothinus.
quote_la: occisus est ab Achilla, cui id facinus erat delegatum

summary_en: Pompey's wife Cornelia and his son Sex. Pompeius fled to Cyprus.
quote_la: Cornelia uxor et Sex. Pompeius filius Cypron refugerunt

summary_en: Caesar, pursuing after three days, was angered and wept when Theodotus offered him Pompey's head and ring, and entered riotous Alexandria without danger.
quote_la: caput Pompeii et anulum obtulisset, infensus est et inlacrimavit

summary_en: Caesar, created dictator, restored Cleopatra to the kingdom of Egypt and at great risk defeated Ptolemy, who made war at the urging of the same men who had killed Pompey; Ptolemy sank in a small boat in the Nile while fleeing.
quote_la: Caesar dictator creatus Cleopatram in regnum Aegypti reduxit

summary_en: The book also contains M. Cato's laborious march with his legions through the deserts of Africa.
quote_la: laboriosum M. Catonis in Africa per deserta cum legionibus iter

summary_en: A war was waged by Cn. Domitius against Pharnaces with little success.
quote_la: bellum a Cn. Domitio adversus Pharnacen parum prospere gestum

summary_en: With the Pompeian party consolidated in Africa, its command was conferred on P. Scipio, Cato yielding although the command was offered to him equally.
quote_la: imperium earum P. Scipioni delatum est

summary_en: When destruction of the city of Utica was debated because of its goodwill toward Caesar and M. Cato had prevented it, its protection and custody were entrusted to Cato.
quote_la: tutela eius et custodia mandata est Catoni

summary_en: Cn. Pompeius, son of Magnus, gathered forces in Spain, whose command neither Afranius nor Petreius wished to take, and renewed the war against Caesar.
quote_la: Cn. Pompeius Magni filius in Hispania contractis viribus

summary_en: Pharnaces, son of Mithridates and king of Pontus, was defeated without any delay of war.
quote_la: Pharnaces Mithridatis filius, rex Ponti, sine ulla belli mora victus est

summary_en: When seditions were stirred at Rome by the tribune of the plebs P. Dolabella proposing a law on debt cancellation and the plebs rioted, soldiers brought into the city by M. Antonius, master of the horse, killed eight hundred of the plebs.
quote_la: inductis a M. Antonio magistro equitum in urbem militibus octingenti ex plebe caesi sunt

summary_en: Caesar granted discharge to veterans who demanded it with mutiny.
quote_la: Caesar veteranis cum seditione missionem postulantibus dedit

summary_en: Caesar crossed to Africa and fought at great hazard against the forces of king Juba.
quote_la: adversus copias Iubae regis cum discrimine magno pugnavit

summary_en: Caecilius Bassus, a Roman knight of the Pompeian party, stirred war in Syria; Sextus Caesar was abandoned by his legion, which went over to Bassus, and was killed.
quote_la: bellum in Syria Caecilius Bassus, eques Romanus Pompeianarum partium, excitavit

summary_en: Caesar defeated the praetor Scipio and Juba at Thapsus and stormed their camps.
quote_la: Caesar Scipionem praetorem Iubamque vicit ad Thapsum castris eorum expugnatis

summary_en: Cato, hearing the news, stabbed himself at Utica, and when his son intervened and he was being treated, he tore open the wound and died in the forty-eighth year of his age.
quote_la: rescisso vulnere expiravit, anno aetatis quadragesimo octavo

summary_en: Petreius killed Juba and himself.
quote_la: Petreius Iubam seque interfecit

summary_en: P. Scipio, surrounded on his ship, added to an honorable death the words that the commander was well, when the enemy asked for the commander.
quote_la: P. Scipio in nave circumventus honestae morti vocem quoque adiecit

summary_en: Faustus and Afranius were killed.
quote_la: Faustus et Afranius occisi

summary_en: Pardon was given to Cato's son.
quote_la: Catonis filio venia data

summary_en: Brutus, Caesar's legate, defeated the rebelling Bellovaci in battle in Gaul.
quote_la: Brutus legatus Caesaris in Gallia Bellovacos rebellantes proelio vicit

summary_en: Caesar celebrated four triumphs, over Gaul, Egypt, Pontus, and Africa, and gave a banquet and spectacles of every kind.
quote_la: Caesar quattuor triumphos duxit, ex Gallia, ex Aegypto, ex Ponto, ex Africa

summary_en: At the senate's request Caesar granted return to the consular M. Marcellus, who could not enjoy the benefit, being killed at Athens by his client Cn. Magius.
quote_la: a Cn. Magio cliente suo Athenis occisus

summary_en: Caesar held a revision of the census, in which CL heads of citizens were registered.
quote_la: recensum egit, quo censa sunt civium capita CL

summary_en: Setting out to Spain against Cn. Pompeius, after many expeditions on both sides and several cities stormed, Caesar gained final victory at great hazard at the city of Munda.
quote_la: summam victoriam cum magno discrimine ad Mundam urbem consecutus est

summary_en: Sextus Pompeius escaped.
quote_la: consecutus est. Pompeius, Sex. effugit

summary_en: Caesar celebrated a fifth triumph, from Spain.
quote_la: Caesar ex Hispania quintum triumphum egit

summary_en: Very many and very great honors were decreed to Caesar by the senate, among them that he be called father of his country and be sacrosanct and dictator in perpetuity.
quote_la: ut parens patriae appellaretur et sacrosanctus ac dictator in perpetuum esset

summary_en: Caesar incurred ill-will because he did not rise for the senate conferring honors, because he placed on his chair the diadem set on his head by the consul M. Antonius running among the Luperci, and because the tribunes Epidius Marullus and Caesetius Flavus were deprived of their power for stirring odium against him as aspiring to kingship.
quote_la: diadema capiti suo impositum in sella reposuit

summary_en: A conspiracy was formed against Caesar, headed by M. Brutus and C. Cassius and, from Caesar's own party, Dec. Brutus and C. Trebonius, and he was killed in Pompey's senate-house with twenty-three wounds.
quote_la: in Pompeii curia occisus est viginti tribus vulneribus

summary_en: The Capitol was occupied by Caesar's assassins; after the senate decreed oblivion for the killing and hostages were received from the children of Antonius and Lepidus, the conspirators came down from the Capitol.
quote_la: oblivione deinde caedis eius a senatu decreta

summary_en: By Caesar's will C. Octavius, his sister's grandson, was instituted heir to half his estate and adopted into his name.
quote_la: heres ex parte dimidia institutus est C. Octavius, sororis nepos

summary_en: While Caesar's body was being carried to the Campus Martius, it was cremated by the plebs before the rostra.
quote_la: a plebe ante rostra crematum est

summary_en: The honor of the dictatorship was abolished in perpetuity.
quote_la: dictaturae honos in perpetuum sublatus est

summary_en: Chamates, a man of lowest station who claimed to be the son of C. Marius, was put to death for stirring seditions among the credulous plebs.
quote_la: qui se C. Marii filium ferebat

summary_en: C. Octavius came to Rome from Epirus, where Caesar had sent him ahead for the intended Macedonian war, was received with favorable omens, and took the name of Caesar.
quote_la: ominibusque prosperis exceptus et nomen Caesaris sumpsit

summary_en: In the confusion and tumult M. Lepidus seized the chief pontificate.
quote_la: M. Lepidus pontificatum maximum intercepit

summary_en: The consul M. Antonius dominated violently, carried a law on the exchange of provinces by force, and treated Caesar with great injuries; Caesar, to gain strength for himself and the republic against him, roused the veterans settled in colonies.
quote_la: legemque de permutatione provinciarum per vim tulisset

summary_en: The fourth and Martian legions transferred their standards from Antonius to Caesar, and afterwards many more defected because of M. Antonius' savagery in butchering suspected men in his camps.
quote_la: legiones quoque quarta et Martia signa ab Antonio ad Caesarem tulerunt

summary_en: Dec. Brutus occupied Mutina with his army to resist Antonius, who sought Cisalpine Gaul.
quote_la: Mutinam cum exercitu occupavit

summary_en: The book also contains the movements of men of both parties to take up provinces and the preparations for war.
quote_la: discursum utriusque partis virorum ad accipiendas provincias apparatusque belli continet

summary_en: M. Brutus in Greece, under pretext of the republic and of the war undertaken against M. Antonius, brought into his power the army commanded by P. Vatinius together with the province.
quote_la: exercitum, cui P. Vatinius praeerat, cum provincia in potestatem suam redegit

summary_en: C. Caesar, who as a private citizen had taken up arms for the republic, was given imperium as propraetor by the senate with consular ornaments, and it was added that he be a senator.
quote_la: pro praetore imperium a senatu datum est cum consularibus ornamentis

summary_en: M. Antonius besieged Dec. Brutus at Mutina, and envoys sent to him by the senate concerning peace accomplished little toward settling it.
quote_la: M. Antonius Dec. Brutum Mutinae obsedit

summary_en: The Roman people put on military cloaks.
quote_la: populus Romanus saga sumpsit

summary_en: M. Brutus in Epirus subjected the praetor C. Antonius with his army to his power.
quote_la: M. Brutus in Epiro C. Antonium praetorem cum exercitu potestati suae subegit

summary_en: C. Trebonius was killed in Asia by the treachery of P. Dolabella.
quote_la: C. Trebonius in Asia fraude P. Dolabellae occisus est

summary_en: For that crime Dolabella was judged a public enemy by the senate.
quote_la: ob id facinus Dolabella hostis a senatu iudicatus est

summary_en: When the consul Pansa had fought unsuccessfully against Antonius, the consul A. Hirtius arrived with his army, routed M. Antonius' forces, and equalized the fortune of both sides.
quote_la: A. Hirtius consul cum exercitu superventiens fusis M. Antonii copiis

summary_en: Antonius, defeated by Hirtius and Caesar, fled to Gaul and joined to himself M. Lepidus with the legions under him, and was declared an enemy by the senate together with all within his lines.
quote_la: victus deinde ab Hirtio et Caesare Antonius in Galliam confugit

summary_en: A. Hirtius, who fell in the enemy camp after the victory, and C. Pansa, who died of the wound received in the unsuccessful battle, were buried in the Campus Martius.
quote_la: C. Pansa ex vulnere, quod in adverso proelio exceperat, defunctus

summary_en: The senate was ungrateful toward C. Caesar, the sole survivor of the three leaders, decreeing the honor of a triumph to Dec. Brutus, freed from the siege of Mutina by Caesar, while making insufficient acknowledgment of Caesar and his soldiers.
quote_la: Dec. Bruto obsidione Mutinensi a Caesare liberato triumphi honore decreto

summary_en: C. Caesar, reconciled with M. Antonius through M. Lepidus, came to Rome with his army and, his opponents cowed by his arrival, was elected consul at nineteen years of age.
quote_la: cum XVIIII annos haberet, consul creatus est

summary_en: C. Caesar as consul carried a law establishing a court of inquiry against those by whose agency his father had been killed; prosecuted under it, M. Brutus, C. Cassius, and Dec. Brutus were condemned in their absence.
quote_la: postulatique ea lege M. Brutus C. Cassius Dec. Brutus absentes damnati sunt

summary_en: Asinius Pollio and Munatius Plancus with their armies also joined and enlarged the forces of M. Antonius.
quote_la: Asinius quoque Pollio et Munatius Plancus cum exercitibus suis adiuncti

summary_en: Dec. Brutus, whom the senate had ordered to pursue Antonius, was abandoned by his legions and, by order of Antonius into whose power he had come, was killed by a Sequanian.
quote_la: relictus a legionibus suis, iussu Antonii, in cuius potestatem venerat

summary_en: C. Caesar made peace with Antonius and Lepidus on terms that the three of them be triumvirs for settling the republic for five years and that each proscribe his own enemies.
quote_la: tresviri rei publicae constituendae per quinquennium essent ipse et Lepidus et Antonius

summary_en: In that proscription were very many Roman knights and the names of CXXX senators, among them L. Paulus, brother of M. Lepidus, L. Caesar, uncle of Antonius, and M. Cicero.
quote_la: plurimi equites Romani, CXXX senatorum nomina fuerunt

summary_en: Cicero was killed by the legionary soldier Popillius at sixty-three years of age, and his head together with his right hand was set on the rostra.
quote_la: caput quoque cum dextra manu in rostris positum est

summary_en: The book also contains the deeds done by M. Brutus in Greece.
quote_la: res a M. Bruto in Graecia gestas continet

summary_en: C. Cassius, charged by the senate to pursue in war Dolabella, who had been judged an enemy, brought Syria with its three armies into his power and forced Dolabella, besieged in the city of Laodicea, to die.
quote_la: Dolabellam in urbe Laodicia obsessum mori coegit

summary_en: By order of M. Brutus, C. Antonius was taken captive and killed.
quote_la: M. quoque Bruti iussu C. Antonius captus occisus est

summary_en: M. Brutus conducted operations against the Thracians with little success.
quote_la: M. Brutus adversus Thracas parum prospere rem gessit

summary_en: With all the overseas provinces and armies brought under the power of Brutus and C. Cassius, the two met at Smyrna to arrange plans for the coming war.
quote_la: coierunt Smyrnae uterque ad ordinanda belli futuri consilia

summary_en: By common counsel they pardoned Publicola, the brother of M. Messala, who was in chains.
quote_la: M. Messalae Publicolam fratrem vinctum communi consilio condonaverunt

summary_en: Sex. Pompeius, son of Magnus, having gathered the proscribed and fugitives from Epirus and long plundered by sea without holding any place, seized first the town of Messana in Sicily and then the whole province, killing the praetor Pompeius Bithynicus.
quote_la: Messanam oppidum in Sicilia primum, dein totam provinciam occupavit

summary_en: Sex. Pompeius defeated Q. Salvidienus, Caesar's legate, in a naval battle.
quote_la: Q. Salvidenum legatum Caesaris navali proelio vicit

summary_en: Caesar and Antonius crossed with their armies into Greece to wage war against Brutus and Cassius.
quote_la: Caesar et Antonius cum exercitibus in Graeciam traiecerunt

summary_en: Q. Cornificius in Africa defeated T. Sextius, a leader of the Cassian party, in battle.
quote_la: Q. Cornificius in Africa T. Sextium, Cassianarum partium ducem, proelio vicit

summary_en: C. Caesar and Antonius fought at Philippi against Brutus and Cassius with mixed result, such that the right wing of each side was victorious and the camps on both sides were stormed by the victors.
quote_la: C. Caesar et Antonius apud Philippos vario eventu adversus Brutum et Cassium pugnaverunt

summary_en: The death of Cassius made the parties' fortune unequal: having been on the wing that was routed, he believed the whole army routed and took his own death.
quote_la: totum exercitum fusum ratus mortem conscivit

summary_en: Defeated the next day, M. Brutus ended his own life, prevailing on Strato, his companion in flight, to drive the sword into him; he was about forty years old.
quote_la: exorato Stratone fugae comite, ut sibi gladium adigeret

summary_en: Among the dead was Q. Hortensius, who was killed.
quote_la: inter quos Q. Hortensius occisus est

summary_en: Caesar, leaving Antonius overseas with the provinces of that region allotted to him, returned to Italy and distributed lands to the veterans.
quote_la: reversus in Italiam veteranis agros divisit

summary_en: Caesar suppressed at grave peril the mutinies of his own army, which soldiers corrupted by Fulvia, wife of M. Antonius, had stirred against their commander.
quote_la: corrupti a Fulvia M. Antonii uxore milites

summary_en: The consul L. Antonius, brother of M. Antonius, with the same Fulvia counseling, made war on Caesar, took into his party the peoples whose lands had been assigned to veterans, routed M. Lepidus who commanded the guard of the city, and broke into Rome in hostile fashion.
quote_la: L. Antonius consul, M. Antonii frater, eadem Fulvia consiliante bellum Caesari intulit

summary_en: Caesar, at twenty-three years of age, besieged L. Antonius in the town of Perusia, repelled his repeated attempts to break out, compelled him by famine to surrender, pardoned him and all his soldiers, and razed Perusia.
quote_la: obsessum in oppido Perusia L. Antonium

summary_en: With all the armies of the opposing party brought into his power, Caesar finished the war without any bloodshed.
quote_la: bellum citra ullum sanguinem confecit

summary_en: The Parthians, led by Labienus, who had been of the Pompeian party, burst into Syria, defeated Decidius Saxa, legate of M. Antonius, and occupied the whole province.
quote_la: Parthi Labieno, qui Pompeianarum partium fuerat, duce in Syriam inrupperunt

summary_en: M. Antonius, with his wife Fulvia removed as an obstacle to the leaders' concord, made peace with Caesar and married his sister Octavia.
quote_la: pace facta cum Caesare sororem eius Octaviam in matrimonium duxit

summary_en: Caesar exposed by his own disclosure Q. Salvidienus, who had plotted wicked designs against him; Salvidienus was condemned and took his own death.
quote_la: Q. Salvidienum consilia nefaria adversus Caesarem molitum indicio suo protraxit

summary_en: P. Ventidius, legate of Antonius, defeated the Parthians in battle and drove them from Syria, their leader Labienus being killed.
quote_la: P. Ventidius Antonii legatus Parthos proelio victos Syria expulit

summary_en: Since Sex. Pompeius, an enemy neighboring Italy, held Sicily and hindered the grain trade, Caesar and Antonius made the peace he demanded, on terms that he hold Sicily as his province.
quote_la: postulatam cum eo pacem Caesar et Antonius fecerunt

summary_en: The book also contains disturbances in Africa and the wars waged there.
quote_la: praeterea motus Africae et bella ibi gesta continet

summary_en: When Sex. Pompeius again made the sea unsafe with piracy and did not keep the peace he had accepted, Caesar of necessity undertook war against him and fought two naval battles of doubtful outcome.
quote_la: duobus navalibus proeliis cum dubio eventu pugnavit

summary_en: P. Ventidius, legate of M. Antonius, defeated the Parthians in battle in Syria and killed their king.
quote_la: Parthos in Syria proelio vicit regemque eorum occidit

summary_en: The Jews too were subdued by the legates of Antonius.
quote_la: Iudaei quoque a legatis Antonii subacti sunt

summary_en: The book also contains the preparation for the Sicilian war.
quote_la: praeterea belli Siculi apparatum continet

summary_en: Naval battles were fought against Sex. Pompeius with varying outcome, such that of Caesar's two fleets the one Agrippa commanded won, while the one Caesar had led was destroyed and the soldiers put ashore were in great danger.
quote_la: ex duabus Caesaris classibus altera, cui Agrippa praeerat, vinceret

summary_en: Pompeius, then defeated, fled into Sicily.
quote_la: victus deinde Pompeius in Siciliam profugit

summary_en: M. Lepidus, who had crossed from Africa as if for alliance in the war against Sex. Pompeius, also made war on Caesar, was abandoned by his army, and, stripped of the honor of the triumvirate, obtained his life.
quote_la: relictus ab exercitu, abrogato triumviratus honore vitam impetravit

summary_en: M. Agrippa was presented by Caesar with the naval crown, an honor held by no one before him.
quote_la: M. Agrippa navali corona a Caesare donatus est

summary_en: M. Antonius, while reveling with Cleopatra, entered Media late and made war on the Parthians with XVIII legions and XVI thousand cavalry; having lost two legions and with nothing going well, he retreated to Armenia with the Parthians pursuing, in great panic and peril, covering CCC miles in flight in XXI days.
quote_la: bellum cum legionibus XVIII et XVI equitum Parthis intulit

summary_en: Antonius lost about VIII thousand men to storms, which he suffered by his own fault in addition to the ill-starred Parthian war, because he refused to winter in Armenia while hastening to Cleopatra.
quote_la: circa VIII hominum tempestatibus amisit

summary_en: Sex. Pompeius, though putting himself under the protection of M. Antonius, while preparing war against him in Asia was overpowered by Antonius' legates and killed.
quote_la: obpressus a legatis eius occisus est

summary_en: Caesar put down a mutiny of veterans stirred up with great destructiveness.
quote_la: Caesar seditionem veteranorum cum magna pernicie motam inhibuit

summary_en: Caesar subdued the Iapydes, the Dalmatians, and the Pannonians.
quote_la: Lapydas et Dalmatas et Pannonios subegit

summary_en: Antonius ordered Artavasdes, king of Armenia, lured in under a pledge of good faith, to be thrown into chains, and gave the kingdom of Armenia to his son by Cleopatra, whom, long captive to love of her, he had begun to treat as a wife.
quote_la: Artavasden Armeniae regem fide data perductum in vincula conici iussit

summary_en: Caesar subdued the Dalmatians in Illyricum.
quote_la: Caesar in Illyrico Dalmatas domuit

summary_en: M. Antonius, for love of Cleopatra, by whom he had two sons, Philadelphus and Alexander, refused to come to the city or to lay down his command when the triumvirate's term ended, and prepared a war to bring against the city and Italy, gathering enormous naval and land forces and sending Octavia, Caesar's sister, a notice of divorce.
quote_la: neque in urbem venire vellet neque finito Illviratus tempore inperium deponere

summary_en: Caesar crossed with his army into Epirus.
quote_la: Caesar in Epirum cum exercitu traiecit

summary_en: Naval battles and cavalry engagements favorable to Caesar are then related.
quote_la: pugnae deinde navales et proelia equestria secunda Caesaris referuntur

summary_en: M. Antonius, defeated with his fleet at Actium, fled to Alexandria.
quote_la: M. Antonius ad Actium classe victus Alexandriam profugit

summary_en: Besieged by Caesar and in utter desperation, Antonius killed himself, driven above all by the false rumor that Cleopatra had been slain.
quote_la: praecipue occisae Cleopatrae falso rumore impulsus se ipse interfecit

summary_en: Caesar brought Alexandria into his power, and Cleopatra, so as not to come into the victor's discretion, died a voluntary death.
quote_la: Cleopatra, ne in arbitrium victoris veniret, voluntaria morte defuncta

summary_en: Caesar, returning to the city, celebrated three triumphs, one over Illyricum, a second for the victory at Actium, a third over Cleopatra, an end being put to the civil wars in the twenty-second year.
quote_la: tres triumphos egit, unum ex Illyrico, alterum ex Actiaca victoria, tertium de Cleopatra
